styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Dim sum, dai pai dong and Michelin counters, all in a day.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Temples, markets and the harbour skyline.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Peak trails, beaches and island ferries.

stays.why: Best first-timer base: Star Ferry, museums and the skyline view from the promenade. Lots of mid-range rooms.
Heart of the city: MTR, trams, bars and restaurants on the doorstep. Pricier and busier.
Shopping and food at every price, good tram and MTR links. Lively but crowded.
Cheapest of the four, with street markets and cheap eats. Very dense and noisy.

food: Start with dim sum for breakfast or lunch; busy local halls are cheaper than hotel restaurants.
Try a cha chaan teng (cafe) for milk tea, pineapple buns and noodles; expect roughly HKD 40–80 a meal.
Street food in Mong Kok and Sham Shui Po: fish balls, egg waffles and tofu pudding, mostly under HKD 30.
Seafood at Sai Kung or Lei Yue Mun: pick your fish and agree the price and cooking method first.
Book popular restaurants ahead, especially on weekends. Many small places are cash-only; check on the day.
more_time: Add a day on Lantau: Ngong Ping cable car and the Big Buddha, or the beach at Cheung Sha.
Swap a city afternoon for a ferry to one of the outlying islands; check the timetable on the day.
Hikers can spend a day on the Dragon's Back or MacLehose Trail sections; bring water and start early.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the harbour, a market and food district, plus one hill or island day; add nights for beaches and outlying islands.

month_notes: January: cool and dry, highs near 19°C. Best month for walking and hiking.
February: still cool and mostly dry, around 20°C. Bring a light jacket for evenings.
March: warmer and wetter, about 13 rain days. Keep an umbrella handy.
April: mild but humid, with around 16 rain days. Plan indoor backups.
May: hot and humid, 22 rain days. Do outdoor sights in the morning.
June: hot, very wet and sticky, 27 rain days. Expect heavy showers.
July: peak heat and rain, highs near 30°C. Typhoon season; check forecasts.
August: same heat and rain as July. Indoor malls and museums are good bets.
September: still hot with about 21 rain days. Storms can still come.
October: cooling to around 27°C and drier. A great month to visit.
November: pleasant, around 24°C and only 6 rain days. Ideal for outdoors.
December: cool and dry, highs near 20°C. Busy holiday season; book ahead.

climate_guide.summary: Subtropical: mild, dry winters and hot, very wet, humid summers with a typhoon season.

items.title: Best time: October to March
items.text: Highs around 19–27°C with fewer rain days. Best for walking, hiking and the harbour.

items.title: Hot, humid summer (June to September)
items.text: Highs near 30°C and muggy. Move slowly, use the MTR and malls to cool down.

items.title: Very wet late spring and summer
items.text: May to September brings 21–27 rain days a month. Pack a compact umbrella and a rain jacket.

items.title: Typhoon season
items.text: Storms are most likely from June to September. Watch official warnings; ferries and flights can stop.

items.title: Humidity is high
items.text: Sticky from May to September. Light, quick-dry clothes help.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light layers, a rain jacket and comfortable walking shoes; a warmer layer for cool winter evenings and strong indoor AC.

transit.best: MTR metro with an Octopus card for most trips; trams and the Star Ferry for the views.

modes.text: MTR is fast and covers most sights. Use an Octopus card to tap in and out.
Buses and minibuses reach beaches and hills. Tap Octopus on boarding.
Taxis are red for the city. Uber works but supply is limited.
Driving is stressful; parking is scarce and costly. Skip it.
Walking is best in dense districts. The Star Ferry crosses the harbour cheaply.
Trams on Hong Kong Island are cheap and scenic.
The Star Ferry crosses the harbour cheaply; other ferries reach the outlying islands.
